transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Rivera. I wanted to come by and talk with you for a few minutes about your son's care and the developmental screening we discussed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Hello. Is something wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've been reviewing the records and I noticed something that isn't right. I want to be very honest with you about it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with how the referral for the screening was handled in our system. Things didn't go quite right with the scheduling process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I remember we missed one date. I told the office.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I see that you had a conflict with that first appointment. I am so sorry that this happened. Our team is responsible for making sure the follow-up happened, and it didn't.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So he didn't get the test?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the charts. It looks like the referral was marked as finished when it actually wasn't.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really understand. Why was it marked finished?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mix-up in the system. We had an issue with the documentation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does this mean he is behind? My son... he is already struggling.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how worried you are about him. It sounds like you've been feeling the weight of this alone, especially wanting to make sure he gets the help he needs as early as possible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want him to be okay. I don't want to cause problems here. I... I don't have papers. Does this mean I'm in trouble for missing that first date?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are absolutely not in trouble. Your status has nothing to do with this. I can tell you're feeling anxious about how you're perceived here, and I want you to know that you are safe and your son's health is our only priority.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you. But what now? Did he miss a window?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it feels incredibly frustrating to find out that a mistake was made when you're already trying so hard to do the right thing for your child.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is frustrating. I thought it was handled.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should have been. I am truly sorry that we let this slip.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So... what do we do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to work on getting him seen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will look into it. I'll try to get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you call me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what the clinic can do and we will probably get an email or a call out to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't always check my email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Well, just stay tuned for an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just worry he is missing out on things he needs.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely understand that fear. It's an exhausting feeling to worry if your child is getting everything they need to grow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Exactly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm glad you shared that with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Can you tell me exactly what the mistake was? You said the system had an issue.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a documentation error. It didn't go through the way it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But who did it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a general error in the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't get it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the box was checked as done, but the appointment never happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why would someone check a box if it wasn't done?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a complicated system. Sometimes things get clicked by mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know my son is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is going to be okay. We are going to fix this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How do I know it will be fixed this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm on top of it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there a date?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't have a date yet. I'll check on it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to miss another one.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We will make sure it happens.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome. I'll head out now and start looking into this for you.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated under pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and vague phrasing ('things didn't go quite right', 'mix-up in the system', 'documentation error') without explicitly naming the error, and never checks for comprehension.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am so sorry'), explicitly states 'Our team is responsible', and maintains this accountability throughout.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('worried', 'anxious', 'frustrating', 'fear') and references the patient's specific concerns about their son's development and legal status.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders ('I will look into it', 'stay tuned for an update') with no specific timeline, patient role, or prevention plan.
